cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: The Company describes itself as a non-manufacturing procurement, assembly and integration business rather than a vertically integrated manufacturer. Our Business, 'PLANT & MACHINERY, EQUIPMENTS': 'Since, we are not a manufacturing unit, we are mainly engaged in the supplying of Forensic products and assembling of different equipment's and Kits.' BACKWARD LINKAGE: forensic systems and evidence-collection tools are procured through a combination of imports and domestic sourcing. Imports began with Sirchie (USA), from whom the Company 'has obtained representation Certificate ... in India to solicit orders for Sirchie Fingerprint Laboratories'; current OEM engagement is via 'Non-Exclusive distributorship agreement with renowned international OEMs or deal in Purchase order basis', with named OEMs Sirchie (USA), Thermo Fisher Scientific, Invitrogen, Rapiscan Systems, Smallpond, MHC Hardware Software Trading LLC and Seratec. Source countries are stated as 'China, USA, Turkey, Japan, Italy etc.' Import substitution is quantified: the Company 'sourced approximately 65.42%, 85.72% and 91.35% of its raw material requirements locally in the financial years ended March 31, 2024, 2025 and 2026 respectively'; the corresponding procurement table prints Forensic Products & Kits Imported of Rs. 501.39 lakhs / 34.58% (FY24), Rs. 629.01 lakhs / 14.28% (FY25) and Rs. 6,43.82 lakhs [printed thus] / 8.65% (FY26), against domestic purchases of Rs. 948.41 lakhs / 65.42%, Rs. 3,774.42 lakhs / 85.72% and Rs. 6,802.24 lakhs / 91.35%, on total purchases of Rs. 1,449.80 / 4,403.43 / 7,446.06 lakhs. Purchases of Goods represented 85.01%, 81.75% and 54.76% of total expenditure and 70.44%, 67.72% and 48.03% of revenue from operations in FY26, FY25 and FY24 respectively (total expenditure Rs. 8,758.90 / 5,386.43 / 2,647.56 lakhs). LIMITED FORWARD/IN-HOUSE INTEGRATION: kits are assembled in-house at the registered office; handheld-device software development is 'outsourced to third parties under non-disclosure agreements (NDAs)' and hardware integration/assembly is 'either outsourcing ... or do in-house'; fuming chamber and cabinet manufacturing and assembling is outsourced; and from mid-FY25 the Mobile CSI Vehicle model shifted to 'supplying only the digital and scientific kits and outsourcing the vehicle procurement and fabrication work to the local dealers', which the Company states 'reduces capital intensity and working-capital blockage'. Both software prototypes initiated in FY26 (AI-Powered Judicial Assistance Platform, LIMS) were likewise developed 'by outsourcing the development work to a third party, based on the concept and framework developed by the R&D team of Kwick'. LOGISTICS: a dual model - direct delivery from import custom house to customer location for high-value/time-sensitive imported equipment, and central dispatch from the Company's office-cum-warehouse for stocked and pre-assembled kits - executed through third-party (3PL) certified logistics providers. NIL DISCLOSURE: 'We have not entered into any technical or other collaboration as on date.'

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Working capital requirement rose to ₹3,587.13 lakhs at 31-Mar-2026 from ₹2,561.57 lakhs FY2025 and ₹992.29 lakhs FY2024; FY2026-27 requirement estimated at ₹4,442.00 lakhs, of which ₹3,142.00 lakhs is to be funded from the Fresh Issue. Trade receivables grew to ₹2,288.07 lakhs and inventories to ₹1,043.71 lakhs at 31-Mar-2026. Government collection cycles are stated as normally 70-90 days with payments released only after detailed inspection. Operating cash flow was negative ₹260.57 lakhs in FY2023-24.
- Government entities contributed 55.22% of revenue FY2026, 78.91% FY2025 and 86.98% FY2024. Results depend on procurement policies, budget allocations, the tendering process, approvals and timely payment by government bodies; the RHP flags reduced bargaining power from a limited customer segment.
- Top 5 customers were 58.04% of revenue FY2026 (55.43% FY2025, 65.36% FY2024); top 10 were 77.64% FY2026 (78.22% FY2025, 82.61% FY2024). The largest single customer was 23.59% of revenue FY2026.
- The Company relies primarily on purchase orders rather than fixed-term contracts; customers may amend, reschedule, reduce or cancel orders. Some purchase orders carry liquidated damages or specific-performance remedies, and in FY2023-24 the Company paid liquidated damages for a delayed supply. Outstanding performance bank guarantees were ₹592.85 lakhs at 31-Mar-2026 (none invoked to date).
- The single largest supplier accounted for 40.86% of cost of materials consumed in FY2026 (₹3,268.40 lakhs), up from 27.02% FY2025 and 12.50% FY2024; top 5 suppliers 67.74% FY2026. The Company holds only non-exclusive distribution agreements or transacts on a purchase-order basis; exclusive agreements between OEMs and competitors could restrict access to essential products. The Company states it has not entered into any technical or other collaboration.
- Gujarat was 29.39% of revenue FY2026 (20.07% FY2025, 22.77% FY2024) and Bihar 9.02% FY2026 (21.80% FY2025, 34.53% FY2024). The RHP states there is no assurance that dependence on Bihar and Gujarat will reduce in the near term.
- Products are sourced from China, USA, Turkey, Japan and Italy among others; imports were 34.58% of total purchases FY2024, 14.28% FY2025 and 8.65% FY2026. Exposure remains to import duties, currency movements, supply-chain disruption and geopolitical tension; FY2026 foreign currency loss of ₹0.41 lakhs was recorded.
- The RHP states "we are not a manufacturing unit", holds no specified installed capacity, owns no major plant and machinery, and operates both premises (registered office and R&D/demonstration branch office) on short-tenure rental agreements — the branch office being leased from the Promoter. Full manufacture of the in-house handheld devices is not undertaken; software development is outsourced to third parties under NDAs and assembly is done in-house or through vendors.
